newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK stocks end down after shock rate rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK stocks end down after shock rate rise.

text.p: A shock increase in British interest rates pushed London stocks well down at the close on Wednesday but sent the pound surging to a 22-month high against the mark.

The rate hike also took the shine off other European bourses, already uneasy about the direction of interest rates, although figures showing weaker U.S. growth calmed some of the jitters about the pace of inflation in the powerful American economy.

London's bourse, which had registered gains with the rest of Europe in early trading, dropped within minutes of news flashing across dealing screens that the Bank of England was raising the minimum lending rate by a quarter-point to six percent.
British finance minister Kenneth Clarke surprise move wrong-footed financial markets which had predicted he would not risk such a bold move ahead of a general election.
The central bank had been pressing since June for a tightening in monetary policy, arguing that rising economic growth meant there was a risk of a resurgence in inflation within the next two years.
London's FTSE index quickly reversed its earlier gains and registered a loss of 0.75 percent at the close to 3963.9 points as investors digested the impact of increased rates on corporate profits.

But some traders took a positive view. "We think domestic investors will deem this a very prudent move which will probably put off any more drastic tightening in the future. We are still positive on this market," a senior trader said.
Paris and Frankfurt had a mixed reaction to the interest rate developments and ahead of important clues on the health of the American economy which may appear in U.S. employment statistics on Friday.
In Paris, stocks lost the day's gains to close slightly down as questions about the direction of interest rates in Europe weighed on markets.
Investors forgot their earlier inflation optimism based on U.S. figures showing that weaker consumer spending on new cars and other goods slowed the economy's growth sharply during the third quarter.
The surprise rate increase in Britain also produced some caution on the part of investors, traders said.
German shares climbed at first, encouraged by firmer German bonds and a strong close on Wall Street overnight but slipped back to show only a modest gain at the finish.

But trading on Frakfurt's after-hours IBIS index fell by 0.5 percent as German bonds lost some sheen following the surprise raising of the British rate. Nervous investors were expected to keep a beady eye on Wall Street and the data coming out of the U.S. for the rest of the week.

On currency markets, the pound, buoyant over the past month, benefited from the Bank of England's move giving sterling a better return for investors. Sterling surged over a pfennig to 2.4616 marks, a 22-month peak against the mark and climbed to 1.6325 dollars, a 19-month high.
"It's been quite a day, and sterling was the prime mover," said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Europe in London. "There have been some large trades," he added.
The dollar, whose recent strength against the yen has taken it to 42-month highs, came under pressure against the yen on Wednesday, dragged down by heavy selling.

The U.S. currency weakened by nearly a half a yen to 113.89 in late European trading after heavy selling of dollars for yen. The yen's revival had started with sales of Australian dollars for yen in the upper 90s region, dealers said.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was trading around 1.5095 marks and 113.89 yen in late European trading versus 1.5100 and 114.26 on Tuesday.
STOCKS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 29.6 points lower at 3,963.9.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 0.98 at 2,124.76.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 5.11 at 2,678.73.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $378.05 an ounce, compared to London's Tuesday close of $381.50. Silver finished at $4.83, down two cents.
